name: Demai (Doubtfully Tithed Produce — Laws)
notes: Detailed laws of demai: which produce is subject, exemptions, leniencies, and the full halakhic framework beyond the general entry

name: Produce Exempt from Demai
notes: Categories of produce treated leniently or fully exempt from demai laws: unripe figs, jujuba, capers, wild figs, etc.

name: Ne'eman (Trustworthy Person for Tithes)
notes: Laws of accepting upon oneself the status of ne'eman — one who is reliable in matters of tithes; obligations this entails

name: Chaver (Rabbinic Associate — Laws and Obligations)
notes: Laws of the chaver: one who accepts strict obligations regarding tithes and purity; restrictions on dealings with am haaretz; conditions for membership

name: Am HaAretz (in Context of Tithes)
notes: Halakhic status of the am haaretz in matters of tithes: produce bought from him, hosting him, and trusting his declarations

name: Verbal Tithing Declarations (Designating Tithes by Speech)
notes: Laws of designating tithes through verbal formulae, including tithing in advance, from a distance, or while in the house of study; complex formulas for combined terumah and tithe designations

name: Tithing in Advance (Hafrashat Maaser b'Tenai)
notes: Declaring tithes conditionally before Shabbat or before eating, so that the designation takes effect retroactively; especially in context of demai

name: Sharecropping and Tithes (Arisut)
notes: Laws of who is responsible for tithes when a field is rented for a share in the produce (aris); distinctions between Jewish, Gentile, Samaritan, priestly, and Levitical landowners

name: Samaritans' Produce (Kutim) — Tithes
notes: Laws regarding produce grown or sold by Samaritans (Kutim) in relation to tithes and demai; their trustworthiness in tithe declarations

name: Tithing From One Lot for Another
notes: Rules for when one may separate tithes from one batch of produce for another; distinctions between field owners, wholesalers, and vendors of different batches

name: Perforated Pot (Atzitz Nakuv) — Agricultural Law
notes: Status of produce grown in a perforated pot versus unperforated pot in relation to terumah and tithes; perforated pot treated as land

name: Peh She'asar Hu Peh She'hitir (The Mouth That Forbade Is the Mouth That Permitted)
notes: Principle that when the same person both creates a prohibition and permits it, we rely on his word; applied in context of seller declaring produce tithed after already stating its origin

name: Maaser Ani of Demai (Poor Man's Tithe Designation)
notes: Whether one must designate (but need not separate) the poor man's tithe from demai produce; dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and the sages

name: Feeding Demai to the Poor
notes: Leniency permitting demai produce to be given to the poor, workers, and travelers without first separating all tithes

name: Mixtures Involving Tevel
notes: Rules for tevel mixed with common produce, tithed produce, or first tithe; calculations for how much must be separated to correct the mixture

name: Use of Demai for Eruv
notes: Permissibility of using demai produce for eruv chatzeirot and shitufei mevo'ot; reciting blessings and zimmun over demai

name: Produce of Syria — Tithe Status
notes: Laws of tithing produce sold or grown in Syria; when declarations of tithing or Land of Israel origin are trusted

name: Dividing Shared Produce Between Chaver and Am HaAretz
hebrew: חלוקת שותפות בין חבר לעם הארץ
notes: Rules for how a chaver and am haaretz who are partners or co-heirs may divide produce without the chaver violating tithe laws; what divisions are permitted and which are not

name: Agent Reliability in Tithe Matters (Shliach b'Maasrot)
notes: Rules for trusting an agent sent to purchase tithed produce; when agent's report can be relied upon and when not

name: Innkeeper and Produce Exchange (Suspicion of Switching)
notes: Suspicion that innkeeper or mother-in-law may exchange produce given to them with untithed produce of their own; resulting tithing obligations on what is returned

name: Produce Ground by Gentile Miller
notes: Wheat ground at a Gentile miller's mill acquires demai status; contrasted with Samaritan or am haaretz miller where original status is retained
